P1: Renamed to Async forms (Jan 2026): Player:LoadCharacter -> LoadCharacterAsync; BadgeService:AwardBadge -> AwardBadgeAsync; MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> GetProductInfoAsync. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer are NOT renamed (keep using them). The old names still work: they are deprecated but not scheduled for removal, and take the same arguments and return the same values. Use the Async names in new code.
P2: Enable it in Workspace > Server Authority by setting Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (fully released July 2026). It forces: NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem enabled, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled on, and UseFixedSimulation. Client-predicted gameplay logic should live in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation, kept in a shared ModuleScript that both server and client run (the server is authoritative, the client predicts and is rolled back/corrected). Inside it don't Destroy/reparent instances, EquipTool or read UserInputService directly (use input actions). Use time() (the simulation clock) for timing, not tick(), os.clock() or os.time().
P3: Property: Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Timeline: June 2026 opt-in (default Disabled); early 2027 planned to default to Enabled; mid 2027 the property is planned to be removed (IAS-based player scripts mandatory). Server Authority mode forces it on. At risk: code calling require(PlayerModule):GetControls() (and the ControlModule/CameraModule internals), code relying on the old input sinking behaviour of ContextActionService/UserInputService bindings against default controls, and forked/customised copies of PlayerModule/PlayerScripts.
P4: The October 2026 update moves Roblox to platform-integrated chat (TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat): message text is no longer handed to experience code. TextChatMessage.Text returns an empty string, and OnIncomingMessage / Player.Chatted no longer receive the text, so scripts that parse chat (e.g. word-triggered features) break. Custom chat UIs can no longer draw messages themselves; you must use the Roblox-rendered chat window (TextChannelWindow-style customization) instead. Admin/chat commands should be TextChatCommand instances. Planned timeline: opt-in until Feb 2027, on by default Feb 2027, required May 2027.
P5: Since July 2026 limits are per experience (shared by all servers and Open Cloud), scaling with concurrent users, measured per minute: Read 300 + 40 x CCU, Write 300 + 20 x CCU, List 300 + 2 x CCU, Remove 300 + 40 x CCU (some docs show a 250 base; design for the lower). Per server defaults still exist (e.g. write 60 + 40 x players). Per-key throughput: 4 MB/min write, 25 MB/min read, each request rounded up to the next KB. Storage is 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime unique player (compressed). UpdateAsync counts as one read AND one write against the budgets. Overflow queues (30 per type) then errors 301-306.
P6: Because Gems are buyable with Robux, crates bought with Gems count as paid random items, and the Luck Potion is covered too. Show, before purchase, every possible item with numeric odds summing to 100%, reachable from a clearly labelled Info/Details/Odds button near the purchase (not a bare icon). The Luck Potion must state its numeric effect before purchase, and while active the displayed odds must update to the true boosted odds. Per player, server-side: call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync and check ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted (fail closed if the call fails or the field is missing); also check IsPaidItemTradingAllowed for trading crate items. P7: They are new age-tiered account experiences: Roblox Kids (about ages 5-8) only sees experiences rated Minimal/Mild with communication off by default; Roblox Select (about 9-15) sees experiences rated up to Moderate. To be available: the experience must have a completed Maturity & Compliance questionnaire with a qualifying content label and pass selection/eligibility review, and not be in excluded genres (social hangouts, sensitive-issue content, free-form drawing are excluded by default). The creator needs ID verification, 2-step verification enabled, and an active Roblox Plus subscription.
P8: Creator Rewards (replaced Premium Payouts July 2025) pays engagement-based Robux: Daily Engagement Rewards pay about 5 Robux per qualifying active spender per day who plays your game 10+ minutes and it is one of their first few launches that day; Audience Expansion Rewards pay 35% of the first $100 a new user (brought to Roblox by your game) spends in their first 60 days. Rewards have a ~60-day hold before cashing out. DevEx: standard rate $0.0038 per earned Robux (legacy $0.0035 for older balances); from June 2026 US creators 18+ get $0.0054 per qualifying earned Robux. Minimum 30,000 Robux to cash out.
G1: Rules: (1) Assign MarketplaceService.ProcessReceipt exactly once (one handler routes all products). (2) Make it idempotent per receiptInfo.PurchaseId: record processed PurchaseIds (ideally in the same player profile as the grant) and if already processed return PurchaseGranted without granting again. (3) Grant and persist the item plus the PurchaseId together, and only after the save succeeds return Enum.ProductPurchaseDecision.PurchaseGranted. (4) On any failure/doubt (player not in server, data not loaded, DataStore error, unknown product) return NotProcessedYet so Roblox retries later (next join). (5) Never yield forever; never grant in PromptProductPurchaseFinished. Charged-but-nothing: returning PurchaseGranted even when the grant/save failed or the player left, so Roblox never retries. Double grants: no PurchaseId dedupe (Roblox re-calls the callback after a timeout/crash/server change, or on rejoin) or granting in both ProcessReceipt and PromptProductPurchaseFinished.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old one or several servers could write the same key (player data across teleports/rejoins, currency, purchase records, session locks); SetAsync blindly overwrites and can clobber a newer save. It also costs a read + write. Transform rules: it may be called multiple times (retries on conflict), so it must be pure: no yielding, no side effects (don't grant items, fire remotes or change state), deterministic from the old value; return the new value or nil to cancel the write; handle a nil old value (new player); don't mutate shared state outside; validate the session lock/version inside it and return nil if another server owns the data; keep it fast and within size limits.
G3:
Not safe. typeof(gold) == 'number' passes NaN and inf: NaN fails every comparison so `gold < 0` and `gold > Gold` are both false and NaN gets through; it also allows fractional values. Also the check is time-of-check only: gold isn't reserved, so a player can make many offers (or spend the gold) before trades settle, double-spending. Fix: reject non-finite and non-integer values and escrow at creation:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
	if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
	if gold <= 0 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
	if hasOpenOffer[player] or not rateOk(player) then return end
	player.Gold.Value -= gold -- escrow (refund on cancel)
	hasOpenOffer[player] = true
	createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
(gold ~= gold catches NaN; gold % 1 ~= 0 catches fractions and inf.) Re-validate both sides again when the trade completes.
G4: The Animator overwrites Motor6D.Transform every frame when it applies animation tracks, which happens after Heartbeat's position in the frame for rendering/stepping, so your Heartbeat write is replaced (or overwritten next step) whenever a track (the idle) animates that joint. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (after animation is applied, before physics/render), composing with the animated value, e.g. motor.Transform = aimCF * motor.Transform (or motor.Transform * aimCF), rather than replacing it; if you accumulate, reset/restore it each frame (PreAnimation) so it doesn't compound. Edit C0 (or C1) instead when you want a permanent rest-pose/attachment offset (e.g. mount pose, grip offset) that animations then play on top of, or when no Animator is touching the joint; cache the original C0 and set C0 = originalC0 * offset rather than incrementally.
G5: Roblox resolves per joint by AnimationPriority (Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4). The highest-priority playing tracks that animate a joint claim weight first; only leftover weight (1 - their total) passes to lower priorities. The default walk is Movement priority; if your swing was authored/loaded as Core or Idle (or Movement and blending equally), walk wins or splits the arm, so the swing looks weak. Fix: set the swing track's Priority to Action (or higher), play it at weight 1 (AdjustWeight/Play(fade, weight)). Weight: within the same priority tracks blend proportionally by weight; a higher-priority track at weight 0.6 gives a 60/40 mix with the lower layer; at 1 it fully overrides that joint. Only joints with keyframes in the track are affected, so the legs still walk.
G6: Unit mismatch: Blender's default scene is metres (unit scale 1.0), and the FBX exporter plus Studio's importer interpret it as centimetres/studs differently, so you get a 100x factor (1 m exported as 100 units). Roblox recommends: set Blender Unit Scale to 0.01 (or keep metres and build at Roblox scale), and in FBX export use Apply Scalings = 'FBX Units Scale' (or 'FBX All'), Forward -Z / Up Y, Apply Transform/applied scale (Ctrl+A in Blender first), Add Leaf Bones off, Path Mode Copy with embedded textures. In Studio's 3D Importer check the scale/unit settings. Alternatively export glTF/.glb, which uses metres consistently. Never just rescale rigged models in Studio.
G7: glTF stores plain mesh data; modifiers are a Blender-only, non-destructive construct. If 'Apply Modifiers' is off in the glTF exporter, it exports the base mesh (the un-mirrored half, unbevelled). Fix: enable Include > Data > Mesh > Apply Modifiers (or apply them manually). Catch: Apply Modifiers in the exporter can conflict with rigs/shape keys: armature modifiers get baked into the rest mesh, and the glTF exporter skips shape keys (morph targets) on meshes with applied modifiers; also applied normals can change (weighted normals). So apply Mirror/Bevel manually on rigged/shape-keyed meshes, keep the Armature modifier unapplied, and check shading after export.
G8: Stretching: UDim2.fromScale(0.3,0.3) is 30% of width and 30% of height, so on screens with a different aspect ratio the frame's shape changes. Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (e.g. AspectRatio 1) or size with Offset plus a UIScale computed from the viewport, and UISizeConstraint for min/max. Hidden by notch/top bar: the ScreenGui ignores safe areas. Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets for interactive HUD (keeps clear of notch and Roblox top bar), IgnoreGuiInset not used to fake fullscreen, SafeAreaCompatibility = None on new GUIs; use a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None (or DeviceSafeInsets) only for full-bleed background art. Anchor the button with AnchorPoint (0,0) and a small offset padding.

```lua
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=..., max=...}
local remote = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
	local now = os.clock()
	if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.3 then return end
	last[player] = now
	if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
	if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 then return end
	if quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
	local item = Items[itemId]
	if not item then return end
	local data = PlayerData.get(player) -- server-owned data
	if not data then return end
	local cost = item.price * quantity -- price from server only
	if data.Coins < cost then return end
	data.Coins -= cost
	data.Inventory[itemId] = (data.Inventory[itemId] or 0) + quantity
end)
game:GetService("Players").PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```

T2:
```lua
-- key: "player_<userId>" -> {data=..., lock={jobId=..., time=os.time()}}
local LOCK_TTL = 1800
function load(player)
	for attempt = 1, 5 do
		local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key(player), function(old)
			old = old or {data = defaultData(), lock = nil}
			if old.lock and old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - old.lock.time < LOCK_TTL then
				return nil -- locked by another server: don't write
			end
			old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()}
			return old
		end)
		if ok and result and result.lock.jobId == game.JobId then return result.data end
		task.wait(2 ^ attempt) -- old server still saving: wait and retry
	end
	player:Kick("Data busy, rejoin")
end
function save(player, data, release)
	store:UpdateAsync(key(player), function(old)
		if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.jobId ~= game.JobId then return nil end -- lost lock
		old.data = data
		old.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, time = os.time()} or nil
		return old
	end)
end
```
Autosave (refreshing the lock) every 60-180s, save+release on PlayerRemoving and before teleport, BindToClose saves all in parallel, don't let the player trade/use data until loaded. Or use ProfileStore/ProfileService.

T4: FireServer automatically passes the firing Player as the first argument to OnServerEvent. By also passing LocalPlayer, the server receives (player, LocalPlayer, 50): `amount` is the Player Instance, hence 'arithmetic on a Instance value'. Fix the client: `remote:FireServer(50)`. Server stays `function(player, amount)`; also validate: `if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end`. Never trust a player argument sent by the client; always use the implicit first parameter.
T5:
Race: in Studio solo playtest the player (and character) can join before your Script runs and connects PlayerAdded, so the event already fired for them and your handler never runs. Live servers usually start scripts before anyone joins. Standard fix: put the setup in a function, connect it, then loop over existing players:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
	local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
	ls.Name = "leaderstats"
	local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
	coins.Name = "Coins"
	coins.Parent = ls
	ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also avoid yields (WaitForChild, DataStore calls) before the Connect line.

T8: RenderFidelity isn't a normal runtime property: it can only be set in Studio/by plugins before publishing (scripts can't change it at runtime, and setting it in Studio may require re-upload/geometry processing), so script changes do nothing. More importantly, Precise only requests full detail; the client still lowers detail based on the player's graphics quality level, memory pressure and Roblox's streaming/LOD systems (model streaming LOD, mesh LOD on low-end devices), so on lower settings or mobile meshes still drop detail at distance. Studio typically runs at high quality so you don't see it there. Check: the property is actually set on the published MeshParts (not on a different copy), test with low graphics quality, and use ModelStreamingMode = Persistent / Atomic for key models; reduce mesh triangle counts so the low LOD looks acceptable. Note: in my lookup the vault had no note explaining this exact symptom; this is general knowledge.
